items.title: How do we measure historical time?
items.explanation: Historical time is measured using calendars, which track the passage of days and years. The Gregorian calendar is the standard used worldwide, counting forward from the birth of Jesus Christ (1 CE) or backward from his death (1 BCE). It uses 'AD' for After the Common Era and 'BCE' for Before the Common Era. Note that there is no year zero in this system; 1 CE follows immediately after 1 BCE.

items.title: How can various sources help us understand history?
items.explanation: History is understood through multiple sources: museums preserve physical objects like statues and coins; geologists study Earth's physical features; palaeontologists examine fossils of ancient life; anthropologists study human societies; and archaeologists dig up remains such as tools, pottery, bones, and bricks to reconstruct the past.

items.title: How did early humans live?
items.explanation: Early humans lived in small groups during the Ice Age. They utilized fire for warmth and cooking, which allowed them to survive longer periods without food. This period marked a significant shift from nomadic hunter-gatherer lifestyles to settled agricultural communities.
